portare.gloss: to carry; to bring; to take

meanings.note: Portare a casa literally means carrying home, figuratively wrapping up a win or workday.

examples.trans: Where should I carry these chairs?
Let us bring the result home.

meanings.note: Marks destination, location in cities, or indirect recipient.
Links activities and idioms such as giocare a tennis or a presto.
Often used without an article after a and da: a casa, da casa.

examples.trans: I will call you from home.

meanings.note: Feminine singular definite article (la scena, la regia).
Third-person feminine singular direct object clitic (non la dico, la risolviamo).
Emphasises the whole course or experience of a day, as in Buona giornata!

examples.trans: It has been a long day.

meanings.note: Unstressed familiar 2nd-person singular direct, indirect, or reflexive pronoun.
Movement away from the speaker or toward a destination.
Used in expressions like va bene, ti va, or andare male.
Asks quantity or duration (quanto per Corinna?, quanto ci mette?).

examples.trans: How long does it take you?

meanings.note: Marks beneficiary (per i ragazzi), duration/target (quanto per Corinna?), or reason (scusa per prima).
Adverbial counterpart of buono; in va bene it expresses agreement.
Conversational bridge moving a talk forward or drawing a conclusion.
Temporal sense in narratives.
Familiar singular subject pronoun; darsi del tu means addressing each other informally.
At the present moment; interchangeable with ora in everyday speech.
Irregular verb; past participle detto, familiar imperative di' (fused in dille, 'tell her').
Interrogative or exclamative word before verbs or nouns.
Conjunction or relative pronoun linking two clauses.

examples.trans: They say that it is true.

meanings.note: Everyday synonym of iniziare.
Marks accompaniment, instrument, or attitude.
Indefinite article: un before most masculine nouns, uno before s + consonant/z, una (un') before feminine nouns.
Dramatic unit of a script or film.

examples.trans: In the scene she is asleep.

meanings.note: Absolute superlative (-issimo) of facile.

examples.trans: It is a very easy question.

meanings.note: Imperative senti grabs a listener's attention ('listen / look').
Mi sento a casa ('I feel at home'); sentirsela (te la senti?, 'do you feel up to it?').

examples.trans: Listen, do you have a minute?

meanings.note: Interchangeable with cominciare.
Absolute superlative (-issimo) of difficile.

examples.trans: It is a very difficult scene.

meanings.note: Conversational contrast word, slightly weightier than ma.

examples.trans: It is nice, though it costs too much.

meanings.note: Places a known reason at the start of a clause.

examples.trans: Since it is raining, I am staying here.
Since you are talented, it will go well.

meanings.note: Identity, description, location, and passive/intransitive auxiliary; with ci forms c'è ('there is').
Also shouted as praise (Bravo! / Brava!); fare il bravo means to behave.
Core verb used in many idioms: non fa niente, fare schifo, farsi la doccia, fare il bravo.
Contraction of a + feminine article la; in alla grande it means in grand style.
Truncates to gran before many nouns (in gran forma); un grande means 'a legend'.

examples.trans: He works in a big studio.

meanings.note: Standard expression of gratitude in all registers.
Standard negative particle placed immediately before the verb (plus any clitics).
Adverb before adjectives (troppo italiana) or determiner/pronoun for excess.
Default masculine singular definite article before most consonants.
On a film set, stage makeup and the makeup department; elsewhere, a clever trick.
Contraction of preposition in + feminine singular article la.

examples.trans: In the scene she is sleeping.

meanings.note: Builds general statements (non si fuma, i copioni si cambiano).
Third-person reflexive pronoun (si chiama, si è svegliata, non si preoccupi).
Before a past participle, marks something that happened moments ago.
Before a clause, introduces an immediate trigger.

examples.trans: I will call you as soon as I can.

meanings.note: Reflexive verb taking essere in compound tenses (si è appena svegliata).
First-person singular subject pronoun; usually included for contrast or emphasis.
Marks possession, material, department (stagista di regia), or topic.
Links verbs like dire, chiedere, pensare to a following infinitive.
Standard cinema verb for filming a scene, originally from cranking film reels.
General physical sense.
Stressed on the first syllable (ˈsubito).
In theatre and television, provare una scena means rehearsing a scene before filming.

examples.trans: Let us rehearse the scene together.
We will not even rehearse it.

meanings.note: Reinforces non after the verb (non la proviamo neanche, 'we won't even rehearse it').

examples.trans: I do not even have a minute.
She does not even greet him.

meanings.note: Variant of clitic ti required before lo, la, li, le, ne (te ne vai, te la senti, te l'ho detto).

examples.trans: Do you feel up to starting?

meanings.note: Marks constant repetition or habit.
Agrees with the person or thing described.
Used for fairness (non è giusto), suitability, and tag questions (giusto?, 'right?').

examples.trans: It is not fair like this.

meanings.note: Imperatives match address: scusa / scusami (informal tu), scusi (polite lei), scusate (plural voi).

examples.trans: Excuse me, where is the exit?

meanings.note: Clapping in appreciation for performers.

examples.trans: Let us give a round of applause!

meanings.note: Ordinal adjective; on a film slate, feminines prima / seconda stand for prima ripresa ('first take').

examples.text: Ho visto le prime due puntate.
examples.trans: I watched the first two episodes.

meanings.note: Invariable film-set noun named after the snap of the wooden slate.
Links words or clauses; distinct from accented è, meaning is.
Adds another person or item to what was already mentioned.
Honorific title used affectionately or ironicaly for film directors and conductors.

examples.trans: A round of applause for the maestro!

examples.text: È un grande maestro del cinema.
examples.trans: He is a great master of cinema.

meanings.note: In A presto!, means 'see you soon!'.
